NEW SECTION . 8.97 Confidentiality of communications 3 with chief information security officer. 4 In the interest of facilitating communication between 5 the chief information security officer and other entities 6 concerning security incidents and security breaches, all such 7 communications and any documents generated based in whole or in 8 part on such communications are confidential. Notwithstanding 9 chapter 22 or any other provision of law to the contrary, the 10 department shall not release such communications pursuant to 11 state open records laws, and such communications shall not be 12 received into evidence, subject to discovery, or otherwise 13 used in a trial, hearing, or other proceeding in or before any 14 court, regulatory body, or other authority of the state or a 15 political subdivision of the state, unless the communications 16 are subject to a protective order that prohibits further 17 disclosure of such communications and requires any court 18 filings of such communications to be made under seal. The section of this Act enacting section 8.96. 24 EXPLANATION 25 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 26 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 27 This bill relates to matters under the purview of the 28 department of management (DOM). 29 The bill strikes current law providing for the use of moneys 30 in the technology reinvestment fund for certain technology 31 projects and instead requires DOM to use moneys in the fund for 32 technology projects using factors set forth in the bill. The 33 bill requires DOM to provide a prioritized list of proposed 34 projects to the governor, who must use the list to develop 35 -13- LSB 5269XD (6) 91 sc/ns 13/ 15 S.F. _____ H.F. _____ a budgetary recommendation to the general assembly, and to 1 report completed and ongoing projects to the general assembly 2 annually. The bill strikes the standing appropriations to 3 the technology reinvestment fund and provides that any moneys 4 in the fund shall remain available for two years after the 5 appropriation is made. 6 The bill increases the frequency at which a person 7 performing work for DOM or an individual on the information 8 technology staff of a supported entity may be subject to a 9 national criminal history check through the federal bureau of 10 investigation from at least once every 10 years to every 5 11 years. 12 The bill prohibits the inclusion of certain provisions in 13 information technology contracts and declares those provisions 14 void if present in such contracts. The bill also provides 15 that such contracts are deemed to include provisions relating 16 to state data, requiring the contract to be governed by Iowa 17 law, and requiring litigation related to the contract to be 18 brought and maintained in a state or federal court sitting 19 in Iowa. The bill authorizes the director of DOM to include 20 limitations of vendor liability in information technology goods 21 and services contracts, but sets forth prohibited terms in such 22 limitations of liability. 23 The bill makes all communication concerning cybersecurity 24 between the chief information security officer and other 25 entities confidential and allows the communications to be 26 released only for specific purposes. 27 Under current law, the department of health and human 28 services serves as the Iowa statistical analysis center and 29 maintains an integrated information system for data sharing 30 among federal, state, and local governments. The bill 31 transfers these powers and duties to DOM and grants DOM access 32 to criminal justice information other than intelligence data 33 and peace officer investigative reports maintained by the 34 department of public safety. DOM is authorized to provide 35 -14- LSB 5269XD (6) 91 sc/ns 14/ 15 S.F. _____ H.F. _____ data analysis and reporting on issues that may affect the 1 state’s correctional population and various subgroups of the 2 population, to maintain a multiagency information system to 3 track the progress of juveniles and adults charged with a 4 criminal offense through state and local agencies and programs, 5 and to count and track decision points for individuals in 6 the juvenile justice system, child welfare system, and 7 court system. If DOM lacks sufficient moneys to perform the 8 authorized tasks of the Iowa statistical analysis center, the 9 bill allows DOM to determine which, if any, to implement. 10 The bill states that DOM is not the lawful custodian under 11 Code chapter 22 (open records) for records DOM maintains in 12 DOM’s information technology capacity for other state entities 13 as an automated data processing unit of government or when 14 held by DOM solely for storage for another department or 15 establishment.
